speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any phlegm or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this cough for about three months now, and it produces small amounts of white phlegm. I haven't coughed up any blood, but I do get quite short of breath when I try to climb stairs. However, this is a low-resource clinic. There is no equipment for ECG or labs. You must reach a cardiac diagnosis from clinical findings only.

speaker: Doctor
text: That duration of three months suggests a chronic issue rather than an acute infection. Since we cannot perform labs or ECGs, can you describe exactly where you feel the shortness of breath most intensely, and does it improve with rest? Also, have you noticed any swelling in your ankles or legs recently?

speaker: Patient
text: The shortness of breath feels most intense in my chest when I climb stairs, but it does improve significantly after I sit down and rest. I haven't noticed any swelling in my ankles or legs recently. I want to emphasize that, this is a low-resource clinic. There is no equipment for ECG or labs. You must reach a cardiac diagnosis from clinical findings only.

speaker: Doctor
text: That relief with rest is a classic sign of exertional angina or heart failure. Given the chronic cough with white phlegm, could you tell me if you have ever been diagnosed with high blood pressure or if you smoke? Also, do you ever wake up at night gasping for air or needing extra pillows to sleep?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, I have a history of high blood pressure, and I used to smoke a pack a day for 40 years, though I quit five years ago. I don't wake up gasping for air, but I do find myself needing an extra pillow to sleep comfortably.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Heart Failure (likely due to long-standing hypertension and prior smoking history).
